# Results — Study 846 (Blockbuster Game-Launch Drift)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**"buy the hype into a marquee game launch,"** then ride the momentum or **"sell the
news"**: does the publisher (TTWO / EA / NTDOY / UBSFY) earn an abnormal return running
into, and coming out of, a blockbuster AAA release? Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

*Stamped as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month).
Fingerprint `ba0709a58928` (TTWO + EA + NTDOY + UBSFY + SPY, one combined panel, adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `TTWO` + `EA` + `NTDOY` + `UBSFY` + `SPY`, one combined panel: 3,393 rows, 2013-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 37 marquee AAA launches, 2013→2024, mapped to the publisher whose stock they most plausibly move; real US standard-edition street dates from Wikipedia release boxes / publisher press releases |
| Events resolvable | **33 of 37** launches have publisher+SPY coverage around the anchor (EA 9, NTDOY 9, UBSFY 8, TTWO 7) |
| Excluded (auditable) | **4** ATVI launches (Overwatch, CoD WWII, CoD MWII, Diablo IV) — Activision Blizzard delisted 2023-10-13 after the Microsoft buyout; Yahoo serves no `ATVI` history, so they carry no tradable tape |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (publisher − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); a Newey-West (HAC) *t* on the date-ordered series; Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; per-publisher and sub-era splits; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | Run-up = [anchor−K → anchor]; drift = [anchor → anchor+K], headline K = 20 (~1 month); net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported. Execution lag = 0 (the launch date is calendar-known months ahead) |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for all five legs |

**Survivorship (named on the Signal axis):** TTWO, EA, NTDOY and UBSFY are all **survivors**
— large, still-listed publishers — so there is no delisting bias among the resolved events,
but by the same token the sample cannot speak to a publisher that failed. **Attribution
caveat:** a single blockbuster title is a small slice of a multi-franchise publisher's
revenue (TTWO also ships NBA 2K; EA also ships FC and Apex; Nintendo ships a whole
platform), so any launch signal competes with a lot of unrelated news — a structural reason
to expect nothing.

## The run-up — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE the launch (publisher − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | *t* (Newey-West) | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week run-up (k=5) | 33 | −1.381% | −1.316 | −1.844 | 8/33 = 24.2% [12.8%, 41.0%] |
| 2-week run-up (k=10) | 33 | −1.581% | −1.259 | −1.626 | 13/33 = 39.4% [24.7%, 56.3%] |

The "buy the hype" run-up is, if anything, a mild **dip** into the launch (−1.4% / −1.6%)
— the **wrong sign** for the claim: a hype-buyer going long the publisher into the ship
date would have *lost* to SPY, not won. And it is **not significant** either way
(one-sample |*t*| < 1.4; the HAC *t* is a touch stronger at −1.84 for the 1-week cut but
still |*t*| < 2). There is no anticipation premium to ride.

## The post-launch drift — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER the launch

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | *t* (Newey-West) | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week drift (k=5) | 33 | +0.339% | +0.383 | +0.382 | 18/33 = 54.5% [38.0%, 70.2%] |
| **~1-month drift (k=20)** | 33 | **−0.165%** | **−0.098** | **−0.099** | 16/33 = 48.5% [32.5%, 64.8%] |

The headline **20-day post-launch drift is a clean zero**: −0.17%, *t* = −0.10, hit rate an
essentially even 16/33. There is no momentum to ride out of a launch and no reliable
sell-the-news fade either. The one-week drift is a faint, insignificant +0.34%.

## Per-publisher & sub-era robustness — 20-day post-launch drift

| split | n | mean AR | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| TTWO (Rockstar/2K) | 7 | +1.228% | +0.535 |
| EA | 9 | +0.648% | +0.401 |
| NTDOY (Nintendo) | 9 | +2.766% | +1.164 |
| UBSFY (Ubisoft) | 8 | −5.597% | −0.971 |
| Early era (first half) | 16 | +1.164% | +0.697 |
| Late era (second half) | 17 | −1.416% | −0.489 |

The (already-zero) drift does **not** hold up robustly: three publishers lean mildly
positive and UBSFY leans sharply negative (−5.6%, driven by a few flops — *Star Wars
Outlaws*, *Watch Dogs 2*), the signs scatter, and the two eras **flip** (early +1.16% → late
−1.42%). Nothing clears |*t*| ≥ 2 in any slice — the opposite of a stable, era-spanning
effect.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | right | −1.581% | +0.153% (1.188%) | 0.938 |
| 20-day drift | right | −0.165% | +0.263% (1.647%) | 0.602 |

Both observed means sit **inside** the luck cloud of ordinary random windows on the same
stocks (right-tail p = 0.94 for the run-up — it is on the *low* side, consistent with the
mild dip — and p = 0.60 for the 20-day drift). The moves are exactly what these publishers'
tracking noise produces on any random window — no special launch effect.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 20-day drift *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−0.098**; across all 33 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−0.324, +1.111]** — so no single launch drives the (already-zero) drift, and it never
comes anywhere near |*t*| ≥ 2.

## Tradability — net of costs

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | −1.581% (*t* −1.26) | −1.681% (*t* −1.34) | −1.781% (*t* −1.42) |
| 20-day drift | −0.165% (*t* −0.10) | −0.265% (*t* −0.16) | −0.365% (*t* −0.22) |

There is no significant edge to bank gross, and costs only push the windows further
negative. "Buy the hype" is a *losing* long here; there is no momentum to ride out of the
launch; and timing a scheduled, telegraphed AAA ship on a large-cap publisher is not a
business — even though (unlike an unscheduled event) the date *is* calendar-known, so the
execution-lag excuse never even applies. There is simply nothing to trade.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (drift = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = −0.24 (sd 1.21); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **1/20** seeds —
  the small-sample false-positive rate at n = 32 events with a 20-day AR is honest (~5%), so
  the detector does not manufacture significance on the null.
- **Planted launch drift +2.0% (seed 846):** mean AR moves +2.00% vs the null, *t* = +1.38.
- **Planted launch drift +4.0% (seed 846):** mean AR moves +4.00% vs the null, *t* = **+3.02**
  — the planted drift is recovered with unit slope (each +1% planted → +1% measured), and a
  large-enough bump clears significance. The machinery works; the real tape simply has no
  bump to find.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **None** | The "buy the hype" run-up is a faint *dip* (2-week −1.58%, *t* = −1.26, HAC −1.63, \|*t*\| < 2) — the **wrong sign** for the claim — and the headline 20-day post-launch drift is a **clean zero** (−0.17%, *t* = −0.10, hit 16/33). Both sit inside the placebo cloud (right-tail p = 0.94 / 0.60), the drift does not survive per-publisher (signs scatter, UBSFY −5.6% vs NTDOY +2.8%) or sub-era (early +1.16% vs late −1.42%) splits, and the jackknife *t* never leaves [−0.32, +1.11]. The synthetic control shows a real bump *would* have been caught. Indistinguishable from noise. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank: no significant edge gross or net, "buy the hype" is a losing long, there is no post-launch momentum to ride, and timing a telegraphed annual-scale AAA ship on a large-cap publisher is not a business. |

**In one sentence:** across ~33 blockbuster AAA launches (2013→2024) TTWO / EA / NTDOY /
UBSFY neither reliably rally into the ship date (a faint, insignificant *dip* if anything,
the wrong way for "buy the hype") nor drift after it (a clean 20-day zero), so the finance
version of "buy the hype into a game launch" is a bust — every faint lean drowns in ordinary
tracking noise.
